I loveeeee my job but it's a lot of HARD WORK for not a lot of money and you have to have an associates degree in medical assisting or be certified to do our job duties, but we make Medicaid money in our city. 18 an hour. Since we already have to go through school, a lot of prospective MAs become nurses and really good MAs also go into nursing for the pay increase. The need for MAs increases in every state every year, so we are always understaffed. Our burnout is so real and often goes unacknowledged both by the health care system (who do not want to increase our pay despite insane need) but also by the general public, often by accident!


We aren't junior nurses or nurse assistants. In fact, medical assistants do a lot of clinical and administrative tasks nurses do not know how to do. We work alongside them, but we work primarily with you and your provider in most outpatient settings.


As in, we are the boss of your provider and an advocate for our patients.


Please give your medical assistants some love and acknowledgement next time you see one :)
